Winter service · Condos & commercial buildings
## Elevator pit cleaning for condo & property managers
Salt slush, meltwater and debris end up in elevator pits all winter. We pump, clean and sanitize pits after hours, coordinate with your elevator contractor, and send a before-and-after photo report — with COI and WSIB clearance included.
- After-hours scheduling, minimal downtime
- Water, oil, sludge and sewage clean-up
- Seasonal programs for multi-building portfolios
- 24/7 emergency line: (647) 833-4343

Why Living Water
## Twenty-eight years of not ruining anyone's brick.
Anyone can rent a pressure washer. The difference is knowing when not to use one — soft washing siding, soda blasting heritage masonry, neutralising an acid wash properly. That judgement is what 7,500+ property owners have trusted us with.
- 28+ years serving commercial, industrial and residential GTA sites
- Fully licensed, with $5M comprehensive general liability
- WSIB covered — protecting building owners from liability
- Certified boom and scissor lift operators
- Satisfaction guaranteed: not thrilled? We re-clean for free

### Soft Washing vs Pressure Washing: Which Does Your Property Need?
Soft washing uses low pressure (similar to a garden hose) plus biodegradable cleaners to kill and dissolve algae, mould and mildew; pressure washing uses high-pressure…Read guide →Guide
### How to Remove Efflorescence from Brick, Stone & Interlock
Efflorescence is a white, powdery salt deposit left when water moves through brick, concrete, stone or mortar and evaporates at the surface. Light, fresh efflorescence…Read guide →Guide
### Is Sandblasting Safe for Brick? Media Blasting Options Explained
Traditional sandblasting with coarse abrasive at high pressure is not safe for most brick — it strips the hard outer face, exposes the soft core to water and freeze-thaw…Read guide →

Questions
## Frequently Asked Questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
How quickly can Living Water start?
Residential jobs are usually booked within 2–5 days, and same-week service is standard. Commercial and industrial clients get 24/7 emergency response on (647) 833-4343.
Are you licensed and insured?
Yes. Living Water is fully licensed in Ontario, carries $5 million in commercial general liability insurance, is WSIB covered and ISSA-GBAC certified. We send a Certificate of Insurance to your property manager, condo board or HOA on request.
Will pressure washing damage my driveway, brick or siding?
Not when it is done right. We match the pressure, nozzle, water temperature and chemistry to each surface — interlock, brick, vinyl, stucco, stone and wood all need different approaches. Where high pressure is wrong we soft wash, steam or use media blasting instead.
Do you do commercial and industrial work?
Yes — refineries, plants, silos and tanks, heritage restoration, graffiti removal, sandblasting and elevator pit cleaning. Many of our clients are property managers, general contractors and municipalities. Our crews are certified boom and scissor lift operators.
What areas do you serve?
Toronto and the entire Greater Toronto Area, including Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan, Markham, Richmond Hill, Oakville, Burlington, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa, plus Hamilton, Niagara, Guelph, Cambridge, Barrie and Simcoe County.
Is the quote free?
Yes. Assessments are free and no-obligation, and you receive a fixed written quote before any work starts.

Professional Power
## Why professional power washing?
Professional power washing removes dirt, algae, grease and stains while protecting the surface underneath — because the right equipment, pressure, water temperature and cleaning chemistry differ for every material.
- Restores curb appeal and a fresh, clean appearance
- Removes dirt, grime, algae, grease, stains and stubborn build-up
- Helps protect exterior surfaces from premature wear
- Improves safety by removing slippery contaminants
- Uses professional equipment and surface-specific techniques
- Saves time with efficient, consistent, reliable results

## Which service do you need?
A quick guide to matching the problem to the right method.
ProblemBest serviceTypical method
Dirty driveway, interlock, siding or roofResidential power washingSoft wash or hot-water pressure wash
Gum, grease and grime at a plaza or garageCommercial power washingHot-water pressure wash, degreaser
Tanks, silos, plant equipment, condenser pipesIndustrial power washingHigh pressure, hydro jetting
Rust, epoxy or failing paint on metal, concrete or poolsSandblastingDustless, soda, micro or dry ice blasting
Painted or stained brickBrick cleaning & paint removalChemical stripping, low-pressure rinse
White powder on brick, stone or paversEfflorescence removalMaterial-specific cleaner, controlled rinse
Tags and spray paintGraffiti removalBio-friendly remover, anti-graffiti coat
Water, oil or debris in an elevator pitElevator pit cleaningPump-out, degrease, sanitize
Historic building or monumentHistorical remediationSteam, soda or micro blasting, poultices
Fire, flood, wind or mould damageDisaster restoration24/7 securing, extraction, remediation

Services
# Residential Power Washing in Toronto & the GTA
Your home's exterior, gently restored. Driveways, interlock, siding, decks and walkways washed back to the colour you bought.
Get a Free QuoteCall (416) 663-8000
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Living Water cleans the outside of homes across Toronto and the GTA — driveways, interlock, patios, brick, stone, stucco, siding, roofs, decks and fences — using low-pressure soft washing with biodegradable cleaners where high pressure would damage siding, mortar or window seals.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience
## At a glance
Best forDriveways, interlock, patios, siding, roofs, decks, brick and stone
MethodsSoft washing, hot-water pressure washing, surface cleaners, sealing
Who we serveHomeowners, HOAs
AvailabilityUsually booked within 2–5 days
CoverageToronto & the GTA, Hamilton, Niagara, Barrie
QuoteFree assessment, fixed written price
- 
- 
- 
Ontario weather is hard on a house. Road salt, spring pollen, summer algae and autumn leaves leave driveways stained, interlock green and brick dull. Residential power washing removes that build-up safely, restoring curb appeal and protecting the materials you paid for.
High pressure is not always the answer. It can strip sand from interlock joints, etch soft stone, blow out mortar and force water behind siding. Our technicians choose between soft washing, hot-water pressure washing and gentle media cleaning for each surface — the judgement that comes from washing 7,500+ properties since 1998.
## What we clean at your home
- Driveways, interlock and pavers
- Patios, pool decks and coping
- Exterior and interior brick
- Stone, cement, limestone and precast
- Stucco cleaning and soft wash treatments
- Roofs: cedar, ceramic and metal
- Gutters, siding and windows
- Decks and fences
- Efflorescence on walls, steps and stone
- Sealant removal from pavers
- Professional paint removal
- Sandblasting for concrete and pools
## Soft washing vs. pressure washing
Soft washing uses low pressure and biodegradable cleaners to dissolve algae, mildew and grime on siding, stucco and roofs. Pressure washing — often with hot water — lifts oil, tire marks and deep dirt from concrete and interlock. Most homes need both, and we tell you which surface gets which.
## Sealing after cleaning
Once interlock, natural stone or pool coping is clean and dry, sealing can help it resist stains and fading. We will tell you honestly whether your surface benefits from a sealer.

Questions
## Residential Power Washing FAQ
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
How often should I pressure wash my driveway?
Most GTA homeowners wash driveways and interlock every one to two years, ideally in spring to remove winter salt and again if moss or oil stains appear.
Can you clean my roof without damaging shingles?
Yes. Roofs are soft washed at low pressure with cleaners that kill moss and algae, so granules and shingles are not damaged. We clean cedar, ceramic and metal roofs.
Do I need to be home during the cleaning?
Not usually. We need access to an outdoor water tap and the areas being cleaned. We send before and after photos when the job is complete.
Do you move patio furniture?
Yes. Our crews move and replace patio furniture and protect plants, windows and nearby surfaces as part of the job.

Living Water provides commercial pressure washing across Toronto and the GTA for retail plazas, office buildings, parking lots and garages, schools, restaurants, warehouses and construction sites — removing gum, grease, graffiti and stains while keeping the property open and safe.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience
## At a glance
Best forPlazas, storefronts, sidewalks, parking lots and garages, schools, restaurants
MethodsHot-water pressure washing, degreasing, gum and graffiti removal
Who we serveProperty managers, condo boards, businesses
AvailabilityOvernight and weekend scheduling; 24/7 emergency line
CoverageToronto & the GTA, Hamilton, Niagara, Barrie
QuoteFree assessment, fixed written price
A clean property builds trust before a customer walks in. Living Water serves small businesses and large commercial organizations across Ontario, and many of our clients are property managers, condominium boards and facility managers who need dependable, insured contractors.
We specialise in removing stains, gum, graffiti and hazardous grease build-up, and in restoring brick and concrete. Work can be scheduled overnight or on weekends to avoid disrupting tenants and customers.
## Benefits of commercial power washing
- Improved appearance — clean facades, walkways and entrances help attract customers and protect your reputation.
- Enhanced safety — removing grime, algae and grease helps prevent slips and falls.
- Longer surface life — regular cleaning slows deterioration and avoids costly repairs and replacement.
## Commercial properties we clean
### Construction sites & equipment
Mud, dirt and debris removed from sites, hoarding and heavy machinery.
### Warehouses & factories
Indoor and outdoor washing of floors, walls and loading areas.
### Parking lots & garages
Oil, salt and grime lifted from stalls, ramps, curbs and walls.
### Schools
Exterior surfaces, entrances and playgrounds cleaned safely.
### Restaurants
Patios, sidewalks, dumpster pads and grease-stained areas.
### Plazas & shared buildings
Sidewalks, walls, storefronts and common areas.

Services
# Sandblasting & Dustless Media Blasting in Toronto
The efficient way to strip rust, scale, stains and old coatings and prepare surfaces for painting.
Get a Free QuoteCall (416) 663-8000
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Living Water offers mobile dustless sandblasting, wet and dry abrasive blasting, micro blasting, soda blasting and dry ice blasting across Toronto and the GTA to remove rust, scale, paint and epoxy from steel, aluminium, brick, concrete and pools.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience
## At a glance
Best forSteel, aluminium, concrete, pools, durable masonry, coatings
MethodsDustless wet blasting, dry blasting, micro, soda and dry ice blasting
Who we serveContractors, pool companies, restoration firms, owners
AvailabilityMobile service across the GTA
CoverageToronto & the GTA, Hamilton, Niagara, Barrie
QuoteFree assessment, fixed written price
Sandblasting — also called abrasive blasting — drives a high-pressure stream of media against a surface to remove rust, scale, stains and old paint. It is the fastest way to prepare metal, masonry and concrete for painting, coating or other treatments.
We work for general contractors, pool painting companies, fire restoration firms, renovation and maintenance companies, and residential, commercial and industrial property owners. Our team can explain why a particular blasting method will — or will not — suit your project.
## Why choose dustless blasting
- Efficient and effective — removes rust, scale, stains and old coatings quickly, leaving a clean profile ready for treatment.
- Versatile — steel and aluminium, brick facades, concrete pool shells, machinery, bridges, tanks, and water and sewage plants.
- Environmentally responsible — dustless technology keeps airborne dust down and uses environmentally friendly media.
## Blasting services
### Abrasive blasting
Removes rust, scale, stains and old paint from a wide range of surfaces.
### Aluminium & steel blasting
Media and pressure matched to metal so the substrate is not damaged.
### Wet & dry sandblasting
Chosen per surface — wet blasting controls dust on sensitive sites.
### Dry ice blasting
Lifts coatings and residue without abrasive media or secondary waste.
### Pool repainting prep
Concrete pool shells blasted clean and ready to repaint.
### Epoxy coating removal
Old epoxy floors and coatings stripped back to sound concrete.

Questions
## Sandblasting & Media Blasting FAQ
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Is sandblasting safe for brick?
It can be, with the right media and pressure. Soft or heritage brick often needs micro blasting or soda blasting instead of sand. We assess first and test a small area.
What is dustless sandblasting?
Dustless blasting mixes water with the abrasive media so dust is captured at the surface, making it cleaner and safer for occupied or urban sites.
Do you blast swimming pools?
Yes. We blast concrete pool shells to remove failing paint so they can be repainted.

# Brick Cleaning & Paint Removal in Toronto
Professional brick cleaning and paint stripping without unnecessary damage to brick, mortar, windows or landscaping.
Get a Free QuoteCall (416) 663-8000
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Living Water cleans brick and removes paint from interior and exterior masonry across Toronto and the GTA, choosing between chemical cleaning, controlled pressure washing and abrasive blasting after assessing the brick and the coating — so mortar, windows and plants are protected.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience
## At a glance
Best forInterior and exterior brick, painted masonry, mortar smears
MethodsChemical cleaning, neutralised acid washing, controlled rinsing, micro blasting
Who we serveHomeowners, builders, commercial owners
AvailabilityTest patch before full work
CoverageToronto & the GTA, Hamilton, Niagara, Barrie
QuoteFree assessment, fixed written price
Brick collects years of dirt, staining, paint, efflorescence and other build-up. Removing it is not simply a matter of more pressure — the wrong method can scar brick faces, wash out mortar, etch glass and kill landscaping. Once that damage is done, there is no going back.
That is why we assess the brick and the material to be removed before selecting a cleaning, chemical or blasting method — and always neutralise acid washes properly.
## Brick cleaning & paint removal services
- Exterior brick cleaning
- Interior brick cleaning
- Brick paint removal
- Old coating removal
- Dirt and grime removal
- Efflorescence removal
- Brick stain removal
- Chemical brick cleaning and acid washing
- Sandblasting and abrasive blasting where appropriate
- Brick restoration and surface preparation

Questions
## Brick Cleaning & Paint Removal FAQ
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Can paint be removed from brick without damaging it?
In most cases, yes. We use chemical strippers and controlled low-pressure rinsing, or gentle media blasting for stubborn coatings, after testing a small area.
What is a brick acid wash?
An acid wash dissolves mortar smears and mineral stains from new or old brick. It must be correctly diluted, tested and neutralised to avoid burning the brick.
Do you clean interior brick?
Yes — interior brick walls and fireplaces can be cleaned with low-moisture methods and full protection of the room.

# Historical Remediation & Heritage Facade Restoration
Respectful cleaning and restoration for historic buildings, statues and landmarks across Toronto and Ontario.
Get a Free QuoteCall (416) 663-8000
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Living Water restores historic buildings, statues and landmarks in Toronto and Ontario using heritage-appropriate methods — steam cleaning, soda and micro blasting, wet and dry sandblasting, and lead paint removal — with a working knowledge of the brick, stone and metals used in Canadian construction over the past century.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience
## At a glance
Best forHeritage brick, stone, statues, monuments, copper and aluminium
MethodsSteam, soda and micro blasting, poultices, lead paint removal
Who we serveConservators, architects, municipalities, owners
AvailabilityTest panels for approval
CoverageToronto & the GTA, Hamilton, Niagara, Barrie
QuoteFree assessment, fixed written price
Historic buildings and landmarks are part of our shared heritage. Over time they suffer from pollution, failed coatings, efflorescence and deterioration, and restoring them is far more involved than a repaint. It requires a firm grasp of the construction and artistic materials used in Canada over the last hundred years.
Our technicians approach every heritage project with respect and care, choosing the gentlest method that will work and testing before scaling up.
## Historical remediation services
- Restoration of historical buildings
- Cleaning statues and landmarks
- Lead paint removal
- Exterior paint removal from all surfaces
- Brick cleaning and brick restoration
- Natural stone restoration and cleaning
- Efflorescence removal
- Steam cleaning
- Wet and dry sandblasting
- Aluminium and copper restoration
## Notable project: the U.S. Consulate in Toronto
One of our notable heritage projects was the U.S. diplomatic building in Toronto. Its exterior combined brick, limestone, concrete, precast, granite, aluminium and glass — each needing its own cleaning approach while protecting the building's historical integrity.

Questions
## Historical Remediation FAQ
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Which cleaning methods are safe for heritage masonry?
Usually the gentlest effective method: low-pressure steam, poultices, soda or micro blasting at low pressure, and carefully tested chemical cleaners. High-pressure water and coarse sand are avoided on soft historic brick and stone.
Can you remove lead paint?
Yes. We remove lead-based paint from historic surfaces with containment and safe handling and disposal of waste.
Do you work with heritage consultants?
Yes. We regularly work alongside architects, heritage conservators and general contractors and can complete test panels for approval.

# Fire, Water & Wind Damage Restoration
24/7 emergency response to secure, clean and restore your home or business after fire, flood, storm or mould.

Living Water provides 24/7 disaster restoration across Toronto and the GTA — fire and smoke damage cleaning, water extraction and drying, wind and storm damage securing and repair, and mould remediation — restoring homes and businesses to their pre-loss condition. Emergency line: (647) 833-4343.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience

When disaster strikes, every hour counts. Our team moves quickly to assess the damage, secure the property and start recovery — from a small kitchen fire to major storm damage.
## Fire damage restoration
- Inspection and evaluation — a full walkthrough to assess structure, electrical and smoke- or soot-affected zones.
- Securing the property — boarding windows and entryways to stop weather exposure and unauthorized access.
- Smoke and soot remediation — removing particles that degrade air quality and keep damaging surfaces.
- Rebuilding and restoration — structural repairs, drywall and finishing once the property is safe.
## Water damage restoration
Floods, leaks, burst pipes and failed appliances escalate quickly into mould and structural damage. We find and stop the source, extract standing water with industrial pumps and vacuums, dry walls, floors and ceilings with commercial dehumidifiers, then repair drywall, flooring and structural elements.
## Wind & storm damage restoration
We inspect for torn roofing, broken windows, stripped siding and hidden structural damage; tarp roofs and board openings to stop water getting in; complete permanent repairs; and recommend upgrades that make the property more resilient to the next storm.
## Mould removal & remediation
Our technicians locate visible and hidden mould and the moisture behind it, contain the area with negative air pressure and barriers, remove affected materials, treat surfaces with EPA-approved antimicrobials, and restore the space.

## Disaster Restoration FAQ

Do you respond to emergencies at night or on weekends?

How fast must water damage be dried?
As soon as possible. Mould can begin growing within 24–48 hours, which is why extraction and drying start immediately.

# Elevator Pit Cleaning for Condos & Commercial Buildings
Winter is pit season. Salt slush, meltwater and debris end up in your elevator pits — we clean, pump and sanitize them after hours, with the paperwork property managers need.

Living Water cleans elevator pits for condominium corporations, property managers and commercial buildings across Toronto and the GTA — removing debris, standing water, oil, sludge and sewage, then pressure washing, sanitizing and deodorizing the pit. Work is coordinated with your elevator contractor, scheduled after hours, and documented with before-and-after photos. Emergency line: (647) 833-4343, 24/7.

## Why winter is elevator pit season
From December to April, GTA buildings track in snow, slush and road salt every day. Meltwater runs through door sills and into the hoistway, salt and grit settle in the pit, and freeze-thaw cycles and spring melt push groundwater through cracks and failing sumps. Left alone, that mix becomes corrosive sludge around buffers, rails and pit equipment — and a slip hazard for the mechanics who have to work there.
- Salt-laden meltwater corrodes pit steel, buffers and rail brackets
- Wet debris and garbage become a fire and odour problem
- Groundwater seepage and sump failures peak during thaws
- Frozen and burst pipes flood lower levels and pits
## Built for condo boards and property managers
### Paperwork ready
Certificate of Insurance ($5M CGL) and WSIB clearance sent with every quote — ready for your contractor files.
### Coordinated with your elevator contractor
We schedule with your elevator company so the car is taken out of service and locked out safely before anyone enters the pit.
### After-hours & minimal downtime
Overnight, early-morning and weekend scheduling keeps residents and tenants moving. Most routine pits are done in a single visit.
### Photo report for your records
Before-and-after photos of every pit for board reports, reserve-fund studies, warranty claims and insurance.
### Multi-building portfolios
One contractor for every building in your portfolio, with seasonal or recurring programs.
### Trusted by elevator companies
Some of Ontario's leading elevator service providers refer their most difficult pits to us — oil spills, floods and sewage backups.
## What's included
- Debris, garbage and dust removal
- Standing water pump-out
- Sludge and salt residue removal
- Oil and hydraulic fluid spill clean-up
- Proper disposal of oily and hazardous waste
- Pressure washing and degreasing
- Sanitizing and deodorizing
- Sewage backup clean-up
- Crack repair
- Elevator pit painting
## How a pit cleaning works
- Quote — send the number of elevators, pit photos if you have them, and the building address. Fixed written price.
- Schedule — we book a time with you and your elevator contractor, often after hours.
- Lock-out — the elevator contractor takes the car out of service and secures it.
- Clean — debris and water removed, oil and sludge cleaned up, pit washed, degreased and sanitized.
- Report — before-and-after photos and notes on anything we see, such as leaks, cracks or sump issues.
## Standards and warranty context in Ontario
Elevating devices in Ontario are regulated by the Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA) under the CSA B44 safety code. TSSA's elevator pre-inspection checklist calls for permanent means to prevent groundwater accumulating in the pit, and for sumps in pits to be covered. For newer condominiums, Tarion's construction performance guidelines state that elevator pits should be clear of standing water or fluids and cleaned of construction debris after construction — useful to document during first-year warranty inspections.
Your elevator contractor remains responsible for the equipment itself; Living Water handles the cleaning, pumping and sanitizing so the pit stays clean, dry and safe to work in.

- Condominium towers and townhouse complexes
- Rental apartment buildings
- Office towers and commercial buildings
- Retail plazas and shopping centres
- Hospitals, schools and institutions
- Industrial and warehouse facilities
## What affects the price of elevator pit cleaning?
Every pit is quoted as a fixed written price. The main factors are:
- Number of elevators and pits per building — multi-pit and multi-building programs are priced together
- Condition — routine debris versus standing water, oil, sludge or sewage
- Waste disposal — oily or contaminated water and material must be disposed of properly
- Pit size and depth, and access for pumps and equipment
- Timing — overnight, weekend or 24/7 emergency response
- Extras — pit painting, crack repair or deodorizing

Questions
## Elevator Pit Cleaning FAQ
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
How often should a condo clean its elevator pits?
At least once a year, and more often in high-traffic buildings. Many property managers book a cleaning after winter to remove salt and meltwater residue, and immediately after any flood, leak or sewage backup.
Who is responsible for cleaning the elevator pit?
The building owner or property manager usually arranges pit cleaning. The elevator contractor maintains the equipment and controls access, so the cleaning is coordinated with them.
Do you work after hours?
Yes. We regularly schedule overnight, early-morning and weekend pit cleaning so residents and tenants are not inconvenienced.
How long is the elevator out of service?
Routine pit cleaning is usually completed in a few hours per elevator. Flood, oil or sewage clean-ups take longer depending on volume and disposal.
Do you provide insurance and WSIB documents?
Yes. We send our Certificate of Insurance ($5M commercial general liability) and WSIB clearance with every quote.
Can you clean pits in multiple buildings?
Yes. We set up one-time, seasonal or recurring programs across property management portfolios in Toronto and the GTA.
What causes water in an elevator pit?
Common causes are groundwater seepage, failed sump pumps, meltwater and salt slush tracked in during winter, sprinkler discharge, burst pipes and floor-washing water entering the hoistway.

We pump out the water, remove sludge, oil and debris, sanitize after sewage backups, and provide before-and-after photos for your records and insurance.

## What to do right now
- Stop using the elevator. TSSA warns never to use elevators in a flooded building or where water has leaked onto elevator components.
- Call your elevator contractor to take the car out of service and assess the equipment.
- Find and stop the source if it is safe to do so — a burst pipe, sprinkler, sump or roof drain.
- Call Living Water 24/7 on (647) 833-4343 for pump-out and clean-up.
- Take photos and notify your insurer if damage is significant.
## What we do
- Pump out standing water
- Remove sludge, silt and debris
- Contain and clean up oil and hydraulic fluid
- Dispose of contaminated water and waste properly
- Clean and sanitize after sewage backups
- Pressure wash and deodorize the pit
- Photo documentation for insurance and the board
- Notes on leaks, cracks or sump problems we find
## Common causes of a flooded pit
- Groundwater seepage during thaws and heavy rain
- Failed or undersized sump pumps
- Burst or frozen pipes and sprinkler discharge
- Salt slush and meltwater tracked in during winter
- Floor-washing water running into the hoistway
- Sewer backups into lower levels
## Preventing the next one
TSSA's pre-inspection checklist calls for permanent means to prevent groundwater accumulating in pits. Talk to your elevator contractor and building engineer about sump capacity, drains and sealing cracks — and book a routine pit cleaning after winter so problems are spotted early.

# Efflorescence Removal for Brick, Stone & Masonry
White, powdery mineral deposits removed safely from brick, stone, concrete and interlock.
Get a Free QuoteCall (416) 663-8000
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Efflorescence is the white, powdery salt deposit left when moisture moves through masonry and evaporates. Living Water removes it from brick, natural stone, concrete and interlock across Toronto and the GTA, and is trusted as the warranty service provider for many Ontario stone manufacturers.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience
## At a glance
Best forBrick, stone, precast, concrete and interlock
MethodsMaterial-specific masonry cleaners, pre-wetting, controlled rinsing
Who we serveHomeowners, builders, stone manufacturers
AvailabilityWarranty service for Ontario manufacturers
CoverageToronto & the GTA, Hamilton, Niagara, Barrie
QuoteFree assessment, fixed written price
Living Water has an extensive track record fixing new and old efflorescence problems. We assess the material first and choose the right cleaning method rather than treating every surface the same — especially important for older brick, stone and heritage masonry, where aggressive cleaning causes damage.
## Efflorescence services
- Brick efflorescence removal
- Stone efflorescence removal
- Concrete and interlock mineral deposit removal
- Exterior wall and facade cleaning
- Chemical cleaning where appropriate
- Controlled pressure washing
- Final rinsing and surface clean-up
## Will efflorescence come back?
It can return if moisture keeps moving through the material. New masonry often blooms for a season while it cures. We explain the cause on your property and the right approach — including when sealing helps.

Questions
## Efflorescence Removal FAQ
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
What causes efflorescence?
Water dissolves salts inside brick, mortar, concrete or stone, carries them to the surface and evaporates, leaving a white crystalline deposit.
Can pressure washing alone remove efflorescence?
Light, fresh efflorescence sometimes brushes or rinses off, but established deposits usually need a suitable masonry cleaner followed by controlled rinsing.
Is efflorescence covered by my stone warranty?
Many Ontario stone and paver manufacturers use Living Water as their warranty service provider. Check with your supplier or contact us.

Get a Free QuoteCall (416) 663-8000
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned

- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Living Water removes graffiti from brick, concrete, stone, metal and glass across Toronto and the GTA — usually within the same week — using bio-friendly chemical removers and controlled pressure washing selected for the surface, and can apply anti-graffiti coatings afterwards.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience
## At a glance
Best forBrick, concrete, stone, metal, glass and painted surfaces
MethodsBio-friendly removers, controlled pressure, poultices, anti-graffiti coating
Who we serveBusinesses, municipalities, property managers
AvailabilitySame-week removal
CoverageToronto & the GTA, Hamilton, Niagara, Barrie
QuoteFree assessment, fixed written price
Graffiti changes how people see your building — and removing it is not just a matter of pressure. The wrong method leaves ghosting or damages brick, stone and concrete. We look at the surface, the type of paint or marker and the condition of the material before choosing a method.
## Graffiti removal services
- Brick graffiti removal
- Concrete graffiti removal
- Stone graffiti removal
- Metal surface graffiti removal
- Paint and marker removal
- Chemical graffiti removal
- Controlled pressure washing
- Anti-graffiti coatings
We serve commercial, residential, institutional and industrial properties, including municipalities and property managers who need fast turnaround.

## Graffiti Removal Projects
Real photos from Living Water jobs across Toronto and the GTA.
Living Water technician removing graffiti from a house wallLiving Water technician cleaning a light brick wallTechnician washing a brick wall in high-visibility gear
Questions
## Graffiti Removal FAQ
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
How fast can graffiti be removed?
We typically remove graffiti within the same week, and sooner for offensive tags or commercial clients.
Will the wall show a shadow afterwards?
Fresh graffiti removed with the right chemistry usually leaves no trace. Older tags on porous brick can leave light ghosting, which we minimise with poultices or gentle blasting.
What is an anti-graffiti coating?
A clear protective coating that makes future graffiti easier to remove without damaging the surface underneath.

Marble, granite, limestone, sandstone, natural stone and precast brought back to life without damage.
Get a Free QuoteCall (416) 663-8000
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Living Water cleans and restores natural stone — marble, granite, limestone, sandstone and precast — on homes, commercial buildings and heritage properties across Toronto and the GTA, removing stains, mineral deposits and organic growth with methods matched to the stone.
Reviewed by the Living Water team · November 2026 · 28 years of field experience
## At a glance
Best forMarble, granite, limestone, sandstone, natural stone, precast
MethodspH-appropriate cleaners, low pressure, stain removal, sealing
Who we serveHomeowners, commercial and heritage owners
AvailabilityAssessment before cleaning
CoverageToronto & the GTA, Hamilton, Niagara, Barrie
QuoteFree assessment, fixed written price
Stone collects dirt, stains, mineral deposits and organic growth over time, and heavy-handed cleaning can permanently damage it — especially older or softer stone. Living Water has built a reputation for bringing old, discoloured stone back to life.
## Stone restoration services
- Natural stone cleaning
- Stone stain removal
- Dirt and surface build-up removal
- Stone facade cleaning
- Walkway and patio stone cleaning
- Mineral deposit removal
- Surface restoration
- Stone sealing where appropriate
- Monument cleaning
Every stone is different, so we assess the material before starting. From a small residential patio to a large commercial or heritage facade, we recommend the right approach.

## Stone Restoration Projects
Real photos from Living Water jobs across Toronto and the GTA.
Contained stone balcony and wrought iron railing during restorationTechnician hand cleaning a limestone wall with drop sheets protecting the groundStone house exterior after professional washingPrecast stone copings side by side showing cleaned versus uncleanedModern stone and wood home exterior during cleaning
Questions
## Stone Restoration FAQ
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Can you clean limestone and marble safely?
Yes. Soft, acid-sensitive stones like limestone and marble are cleaned with pH-appropriate products and low pressure — never harsh acids.
Should natural stone be sealed?
Often, yes — especially patios and pool coping. Sealing helps resist staining. We advise based on the stone type and use.
Do you clean monuments and statues?
Yes. Monuments, memorials and statues are cleaned with gentle, conservation-appropriate methods.

Downtown, storefronts, condo podiums and heritage facades collect soot, gum and graffiti that need the right chemistry, not more pressure.

- Heritage Conservation District properties may need approved cleaning methods and test panels before work starts.

Expert Guide
# Soft Washing vs Pressure Washing: Which Does Your Property Need?
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Soft washing uses low pressure (similar to a garden hose) plus biodegradable cleaners to kill and dissolve algae, mould and mildew; pressure washing uses high-pressure water — often heated — to physically blast off dirt, oil and stains. Use soft washing on siding, stucco, roofs, painted wood and soft or heritage masonry; use pressure washing on concrete, interlock and other hard, durable surfaces.
- 
- 
- 
- 
- 
## What is soft washing?
Soft washing applies a cleaning solution at low pressure, lets it dwell so it can break down organic growth, then rinses gently. Because the chemistry does the work, it reaches algae and mould spores that pressure alone only knocks off the surface — so results last longer.
## What is pressure washing?
Pressure washing relies on mechanical force. Professional units deliver high pressure and high flow, and hot-water machines (often called "power washing") cut through oil, grease, gum and tire marks far faster than cold water.
## Which method for which surface?
SurfaceRecommended methodWhy
Vinyl and aluminium sidingSoft washHigh pressure forces water behind panels and can crack or dent them.
Stucco and EIFSSoft washPressure can gouge the finish and drive water into the wall.
Asphalt shingle, cedar or ceramic roofsSoft washPressure strips granules, splits shakes and can void warranties.
Wood decks and fencesLow pressure / soft washHigh pressure raises and furrows the grain.
Heritage or soft brick and stoneSoft wash, steam or gentle media blastingPressure erodes the brick face and washes out mortar.
Concrete driveways and garage floorsHot-water pressure washDurable surface; heat lifts oil and grease.
Interlock and paversPressure wash with surface cleaner, then re-sandRemoves moss and staining; joints are re-filled afterwards.
Commercial sidewalks and plazasHot-water pressure washRemoves gum, grease and heavy foot-traffic grime.
## What happens when the wrong method is used?
- Etched "wand marks" and stripes in concrete
- Sand blown out of interlock joints, leading to weeds and shifting
- Mortar washed out of brick joints, letting water in
- Water forced behind siding and into window seals
- Shingle granules stripped, shortening roof life
## Most homes need both
A typical GTA home combines a soft-washed house, roof and deck with a pressure-washed driveway and walkway. A professional crew will tell you which surface gets which method before work starts.
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Is soft washing as effective as pressure washing?
For organic growth like algae, mould and mildew it is usually more effective, because the cleaner kills the growth instead of just knocking off the surface layer.
Is soft washing safe for plants?
Professional crews pre-wet and rinse plants and use biodegradable cleaners to protect landscaping.
What is the difference between power washing and pressure washing?
The terms are often used interchangeably; 'power washing' usually refers to pressure washing with heated water.

Expert Guide
# How to Remove Efflorescence from Brick, Stone & Interlock
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Efflorescence is a white, powdery salt deposit left when water moves through brick, concrete, stone or mortar and evaporates at the surface. Light, fresh efflorescence can be dry-brushed off; established deposits need a masonry cleaner suited to the material, applied to a pre-wetted surface and thoroughly rinsed. It stops returning only when the moisture source is controlled or the material finishes curing.
- 
- 
- 
- 
- 
## What causes efflorescence?
Three things must be present: soluble salts in or behind the masonry, water to dissolve them, and a path for that water to reach the surface and evaporate. New brick, mortar, precast and concrete pavers contain more free salts, which is why new homes and new interlock often "bloom" in their first year or two.
## Efflorescence vs other white stains
- Efflorescence — powdery or crystalline, often brushes off when dry, reappears after rain.
- Lime run / calcium carbonate — hard white crust, often streaking from mortar joints; needs stronger treatment.
- Mortar smears — left from construction; removed with a properly neutralised masonry cleaner.
## How professionals remove efflorescence
- Identify the material and the deposit — limestone, marble and some precast are acid-sensitive.
- Test a small area to confirm the cleaner will not discolour the surface.
- Pre-wet the surface so the cleaner stays on the face and is not drawn deep into the material.
- Apply the correct cleaner and agitate where needed.
- Rinse thoroughly with controlled pressure, and neutralise if an acid-based product was used.
- Address the moisture — downspouts, grading, failed caulking or missing caps.
## Mistakes to avoid
- Using undiluted muriatic acid — it can burn brick, etch stone and leave new stains.
- Blasting with high pressure — it drives more water in and can damage the face.
- Sealing over efflorescence — it traps the salts and can cause spalling.
## Will it come back?
On new construction, efflorescence often returns a few times as the material cures, then stops. On older buildings, recurring efflorescence points to a moisture problem that should be fixed. Once the surface is clean and dry, a breathable sealer can help on pavers and some stone.
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Does vinegar remove efflorescence?
Diluted vinegar can lift light efflorescence on durable brick, but it is acidic and can etch limestone, marble and some precast. Test first or use a product made for the specific material.
Is efflorescence harmful?
Efflorescence itself is cosmetic, but it shows water is moving through the masonry, which can lead to freeze-thaw damage over time.
Is efflorescence covered under paver or stone warranties?
Many manufacturers treat it as a natural occurrence; some use specialist contractors such as Living Water for warranty service. Check with your supplier.

Expert Guide
# Is Sandblasting Safe for Brick? Media Blasting Options Explained
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Traditional sandblasting with coarse abrasive at high pressure is not safe for most brick — it strips the hard outer face, exposes the soft core to water and freeze-thaw damage, and erodes mortar. Brick can be cleaned or stripped safely with gentler methods: chemical paint strippers, low-pressure micro blasting with fine media, soda blasting, steam, or dry ice blasting, chosen after a test patch.
- 
- 
- 
- 
## Why aggressive sandblasting damages brick
Clay brick is fired to create a hard, dense outer skin. Coarse abrasive at high pressure removes that skin along with the dirt or paint, leaving a rough, porous surface that absorbs water. In Ontario's freeze-thaw cycles, absorbed water expands and causes spalling — faces popping off — within a few winters.
## Safer blasting and cleaning options
MethodHow it worksBest for
Chemical strippingStripper softens paint, removed with low-pressure rinsingPainted brick, heritage facades
Micro blastingFine media at low pressure, tightly controlledDetailed masonry, stubborn coatings
Soda blastingSodium bicarbonate media, softer than sandDelicate surfaces, soot, light coatings
Dry ice blastingFrozen CO₂ pellets that sublimate on impactCoatings and residue with no media clean-up
Steam cleaningLow-pressure, high-temperature waterHeritage stone and brick, organic staining
Dustless (wet) abrasive blastingAbrasive mixed with water to control dustConcrete, steel, pools, durable masonry
## When is sandblasting the right choice?
Abrasive blasting is excellent for steel, aluminium, concrete, pool shells, bridges, tanks and heavy coatings like epoxy. On masonry it should be limited to durable brick or concrete, at low pressure, with fine media — and always after a test panel.
## Questions to ask a blasting contractor
- Will you do a test patch and let me approve it?
- What media and pressure will you use, and why?
- How will dust, runoff and neighbouring property be protected?
- Are you WSIB covered and insured, and can you provide a certificate?
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Can painted brick be restored to original?
Usually, yes, with chemical stripping and gentle rinsing or micro blasting. Some paint ghosting may remain on very porous brick.
Is soda blasting safe for brick?
Soda is much softer than sand and is often suitable for brick and stone, but pressure and nozzle distance still matter, and sodium residue must be rinsed well.
Does dustless blasting create dust?
It greatly reduces airborne dust by wetting the media, making it better suited to occupied or urban sites.

Expert Guide
# How Often Should You Pressure Wash in Ontario? A Seasonal Schedule
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Most GTA homes should have driveways, walkways and interlock pressure washed once a year — ideally in spring after road salt season — with house siding and roofs soft washed every one to three years as algae appears, and decks cleaned annually before sealing. Commercial entrances, sidewalks and parking areas typically need cleaning monthly to quarterly depending on foot traffic.
- 
- 
- 
- 
- 
## Recommended frequency by surface
SurfaceHow oftenBest time
Driveway and walkwaysEvery yearSpring, after salt season
Interlock and paversEvery 1–2 years, re-sand as neededLate spring
House siding / brickEvery 1–3 yearsSpring to early fall
Roof (moss / algae)When growth appears, typically every 2–4 yearsSpring or fall
Deck and fenceEvery yearSpring, before staining or sealing
Pool deck and copingEvery yearPool opening
Commercial entrances & sidewalksMonthly to quarterlyYear-round, off-hours
Parking garages1–2 times per yearSpring, after salt season
## Spring: the most important clean
Road salt, sand and winter grime are corrosive to concrete and interlock and stain brick. A spring wash removes them before summer heat bakes stains in, and it is the right moment to check for frost damage, efflorescence and loose pavers.
## Summer: decks, patios and sealing
Warm, dry weather is ideal for cleaning and sealing decks, pool coping and stone patios, which need dry surfaces to cure.
## Fall: before freeze-up
Removing moss, leaves and organic growth in fall keeps surfaces from staying wet through winter, reducing freeze-thaw damage and slip hazards.
## Winter
Exterior washing stops once temperatures stay below freezing, but emergency work, interior cleaning, elevator pits and industrial jobs continue year-round.
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Can you pressure wash in winter in Toronto?
Exterior residential washing is generally avoided below freezing because water freezes on surfaces. Interior, industrial and emergency work continues year-round.
Does regular pressure washing damage concrete?
Not when done correctly with surface cleaners at appropriate pressure. Annual cleaning helps concrete last longer by removing salt and organic growth.

# Elevator Pit Cleaning: What Building Managers Need to Know
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Elevator pits collect garbage, dust, oil and water over time, creating fire, slip and environmental hazards for riders and maintenance crews. Building managers should have pits inspected during routine elevator maintenance and professionally cleaned whenever debris, oil, standing water or odours are present — and immediately after flooding or a sewage backup.
- 
- 
- 
- 
## Why elevator pits get dirty
The pit sits at the lowest point of the hoistway. Debris falls through door gaps, hydraulic and lubricating oil can leak, and groundwater, sprinkler discharge or sewage backups collect there. Because nobody sees it, contamination builds up unnoticed.
## Warning signs
- Garbage or dust accumulation
- Standing water, mud or sludge
- Oil sheen or hydraulic fluid on the floor
- Foul odours from the hoistway
- Visible cracks or water entry
## What professional elevator pit cleaning includes
- Coordination with your elevator service provider so the elevator is locked out safely
- Removal of debris, sludge and standing water
- Oil spill clean-up and proper disposal of hazardous waste
- Pressure washing and degreasing of the pit floor, walls and equipment
- Sanitizing and deodorizing, especially after sewage backups
- Crack repair and pit painting where required
## Why use a specialist?
Pit work involves confined spaces, moving equipment and contaminated waste. Elevator companies across Ontario refer pit cleaning to specialists like Living Water so their mechanics can focus on the equipment.
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Who is responsible for cleaning the elevator pit?
Usually the building owner or property manager arranges cleaning, coordinated with the elevator maintenance contractor who controls access to the equipment.
How long does elevator pit cleaning take?
Routine cleaning is often completed in a few hours; flood or oil spill clean-up can take longer depending on volume and disposal.

# How to Hire a Pressure Washing Contractor in the GTA: 10 Questions to Ask
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Before hiring a pressure washing contractor in Ontario, confirm they carry commercial general liability insurance and WSIB coverage (and can send certificates), ask how they will clean each surface and protect plants, windows and runoff, get a fixed written quote with scope and timing, and look for verifiable reviews and before-and-after photos of similar work.
## 10 questions to ask
- Are you insured? Ask for a Certificate of Insurance showing commercial general liability. Living Water carries $5M.
- Are your workers covered by WSIB? In Ontario, hiring a contractor without WSIB coverage can expose the property owner to liability. Ask for a clearance certificate.
- How will you clean each surface? A professional distinguishes soft washing, hot-water pressure washing and blasting.
- Will you test first? Essential for brick, stone, heritage and paint removal.
- How will you protect plants, windows, vehicles and neighbours?
- How do you manage wash water and runoff? Municipal sewer bylaws restrict what can enter storm drains.
- Is the quote fixed and in writing? It should state method, scope, timing and price.
- Do you have photos of similar jobs?
- What happens if I'm not satisfied? Look for a re-clean guarantee.
- Are your crews certified for lifts and work at height? Needed for multi-storey facades.
## Red flags
- Cash-only, no written quote
- No insurance certificate or WSIB clearance
- "One pressure for everything"
- Pressure to decide on the spot

Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.

## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Why does WSIB matter when hiring a contractor?
If an uncovered worker is injured on your property, you may face liability. A WSIB clearance certificate confirms the contractor's account is in good standing.
Should a pressure washing quote be free?
Most reputable contractors provide free assessments and fixed written quotes; Living Water does.

# Winter Elevator Pit Checklist for Condo & Property Managers
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: In winter, condo and property managers should ask their elevator contractor to report pit conditions at every maintenance visit, watch for water, salt residue, odours and debris, keep entrance matting and sill areas clean to limit meltwater, test sump pumps before the thaw, and book a professional pit cleaning after winter — or immediately after any flood, leak or sewage backup.
- 
- 
- 
- 
- 
## Why winter is hard on elevator pits
Snow and slush tracked into lobbies melts at the elevator sill and runs into the hoistway, carrying road salt and grit. Freeze-thaw cycles and spring melt raise groundwater, and frozen pipes and sprinklers can flood lower levels. The result is corrosive, salty sludge around buffers and rail brackets.
## Monthly winter checklist
- Ask your elevator contractor to note pit condition (water, debris, oil) on every service report.
- Check lobby and garage entrances: matting in place, sill areas swept and dry.
- Watch for odours, damp marks or salt staining at landing doors.
- Confirm the pit sump pump (if present) runs and its cover is secure.
- Check for leaks from garage ceilings, sprinkler lines and drains near the hoistway.
- Keep a log with photos — useful for reserve-fund planning and warranty or insurance claims.
## When to book a pit cleaning
- After winter, to remove salt, grit and meltwater residue
- Immediately after any flood, leak, sewage backup or oil spill
- When your elevator contractor reports debris, water or oil
- Before first-year Tarion warranty inspections in new condominiums
## What the rules say
Ontario elevators are regulated by TSSA under the CSA B44 code. TSSA's pre-inspection checklist calls for permanent means to prevent groundwater accumulating in pits and for sumps to be covered, and TSSA warns never to use elevators in a flooded building. Tarion's guidelines for new condominiums state pits should be clear of standing water and cleaned of construction debris.
## Budgeting tip
Ask for a fixed written quote per pit and a seasonal program across all your buildings. A post-winter clean and an annual clean are a common pattern; emergency pump-outs are billed separately.
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Should elevator pits be cleaned in winter or spring?
Both have a place: emergency pump-outs happen whenever water appears, and a scheduled clean after winter removes the season's salt and meltwater residue.
Can our cleaning staff clean the elevator pit?
Entering a pit requires the elevator to be taken out of service and secured by the elevator contractor, so pit cleaning should be coordinated with them and done by trained contractors.

# How to Clean and Re-Sand Interlock Pavers
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Interlock is cleaned by pre-treating stains and organic growth, washing with a rotary surface cleaner (not a bare wand) to avoid stripes, flushing out old joint sand and debris, letting the pavers dry completely, then sweeping new polymeric sand into the joints and activating it with a light mist. Sealing is optional and protects colour and helps resist stains.
- 
- 
- 
## Why interlock gets dirty and weedy
Joint sand washes out over time, leaving gaps where soil, seeds and moss settle. Oil drips, tire marks, rust from patio furniture and winter salt add stains, and new pavers can bloom with efflorescence.
## Step-by-step professional process
- Inspect for sunken or broken pavers and drainage problems.
- Pre-treat oil, rust and organic stains with suitable cleaners.
- Surface-clean with a rotary cleaner for an even, stripe-free finish.
- Flush the joints to remove old sand, weeds and moss.
- Rinse and dry — polymeric sand needs dry pavers and dry joints.
- Re-sand with polymeric sand, compact, and sweep off the surface.
- Activate with a fine mist so the sand hardens without hazing.
- Seal (optional) once fully cured, if the surface benefits.
## Common mistakes
- Using a narrow wand tip — leaves stripes and erodes the paver face.
- Applying polymeric sand to damp pavers — causes haze that is hard to remove.
- Sealing over efflorescence or damp pavers — traps moisture and whitens the sealer.
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
How often should interlock be re-sanded?
Typically every few years, or whenever joints look empty or weeds start appearing. Polymeric sand lasts longer than regular sand.
Should I seal my interlock?
Sealing is optional. It can enrich colour and make stains easier to clean, but it must be applied to clean, dry pavers with no efflorescence.

Expert Guide
# How to Remove Paint from Brick Without Damaging It
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: The safest way to remove paint from brick is a chemical paint stripper matched to the coating, left to dwell (often under a cover), then removed with low-pressure rinsing or scraping — with gentle micro or soda blasting only for stubborn residue. Avoid high-pressure washing and coarse sandblasting, which strip the brick's fired face and lead to water damage.
- 
- 
- 
- 
## Start with a test patch
Paint type, the number of layers and the brick itself all affect results. A small test area shows which stripper works, how long it needs, and whether any ghosting will remain — before the whole wall is committed.
## Methods compared
MethodRisk to brickNotes
Chemical stripper + low-pressure rinseLowThe standard approach for most painted brick.
Micro / soda blastingLow–mediumFor residue in pores and textured brick, at controlled pressure.
SteamLowHelps soften some coatings on heritage masonry.
High-pressure washing aloneHighRarely removes paint and erodes brick and mortar.
Coarse sandblastingVery highDestroys the brick face; avoid on clay brick.
## Lead paint
Older buildings may have lead-based paint. It must be removed with containment and proper waste handling — not dry-scraped or blasted into the open air.
## After paint removal
Once stripped and rinsed, brick should be left breathable. Repointing failed mortar joints and fixing water sources helps the restored brick last.
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Can all paint be removed from brick?
Most coatings can be removed. Very porous brick may keep faint ghosting of the old paint, which a test patch will reveal.
Is it better to repaint brick instead?
Painted brick needs repainting every several years and can trap moisture. Stripping restores a low-maintenance, breathable surface.

# Graffiti Removal Guide: Brick, Concrete, Stone & Metal
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Graffiti is best removed quickly with a remover matched to the paint and the surface — solvent-based removers for spray paint and markers, followed by controlled low-to-medium pressure rinsing — rather than high pressure alone, which drives paint deeper into porous brick and concrete. Anti-graffiti coatings make future tags much easier to remove.
- 
- 
- 
## Why fast removal matters
Fresh paint sits closer to the surface and comes off more cleanly. The longer it cures, the deeper it penetrates porous materials, and quickly removed tags are less likely to attract more.
## Approach by surface
SurfaceTypical approach
BrickRemover dwell, then low-pressure hot rinse; poultice for ghosting
ConcreteRemover plus hot-water pressure rinse
Natural stonepH-appropriate remover, gentle rinse, poultice if needed
Metal & painted surfacesMild solvent that lifts tag but not factory finish
GlassSolvent and blade; etched graffiti needs polishing or film
## Anti-graffiti coatings
Sacrificial coatings come off with the graffiti and are re-applied; permanent coatings let tags be wiped or washed off repeatedly. Both should be breathable on masonry.
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Will graffiti removal leave a shadow?
Fresh graffiti usually leaves no trace. Old tags on porous brick may leave light ghosting, reduced with poultices or gentle blasting.
Who removes graffiti on private property in Toronto?
Property owners are generally responsible for removing graffiti from their buildings; check your municipality's current graffiti bylaw for timelines.

# What Affects the Cost of Pressure Washing in Toronto?
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: Pressure washing prices in the GTA depend mainly on the area and type of surface, how heavy the staining or growth is, the cleaning method required (soft wash, hot water, chemical or blasting), access and height (ladders, lifts, containment), extras like re-sanding or sealing, and scheduling such as after-hours or emergency work. A site-specific, fixed written quote is the only reliable number.
- 
- 
- 
## The main cost factors
FactorWhy it matters
Size of the areaMore square footage means more time, water and product.
Surface typeDelicate surfaces (heritage brick, limestone, cedar) need slower, gentler methods.
Level of stainingOil, rust, paint, efflorescence and deep moss need pre-treatment or multiple passes.
MethodSoft washing, hot-water washing, chemical cleaning and media blasting use different equipment and materials.
Access & heightLadders, boom or scissor lifts, scaffolding and containment add set-up time.
Protection & runoffCovering plants, windows and vehicles, and managing wash water.
ExtrasPolymeric sand, sealing, anti-graffiti coatings, repairs.
SchedulingOvernight, weekend or 24/7 emergency work.
## How to get an accurate quote
- Send photos of each surface and any problem areas.
- Give approximate dimensions and your postal code.
- Mention access limits — tight side yards, heights, parking.
- Ask for a fixed written quote with method and scope, not an hourly estimate.
## Why the cheapest quote can cost more
Damage from the wrong method — etched concrete, washed-out mortar, stripped shingles, burned brick — is expensive or impossible to reverse. Compare insurance, WSIB coverage and method, not just price.

Expert Guide
# After a Fire: First Steps for Property Owners
By the Living Water team · 28 years cleaning and restoring GTA properties · Updated November 2026
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
Short answer: After a fire, wait until the fire department confirms the building is safe to enter, contact your insurance company right away, document the damage with photos before anything is moved, secure the property against weather and entry, and start professional smoke, soot and water clean-up quickly — soot and firefighting water keep causing damage the longer they sit.
- 
- 
- 
## First 24 hours
- Safety first — only re-enter when officials say it is safe; utilities may need inspection before reconnection.
- Call your insurer and ask how they want the claim documented.
- Photograph everything before cleaning or removing items.
- Secure the property — board windows and doors, tarp the roof.
- Remove standing water from firefighting to limit mould.
## Why soot and smoke need fast action
Soot is acidic and can discolour and etch surfaces, and smoke odour penetrates porous materials. Early cleaning limits permanent damage and keeps restoration costs down.
## What professional restoration includes
- Damage assessment and a written scope
- Board-up and weather protection
- Water extraction and drying
- Smoke and soot remediation on structure and surfaces
- Exterior soot cleaning on brick, stone and siding
- Repairs and rebuilding
## Need help with your property?
Living Water has cleaned and restored 7,500+ properties across Toronto and the GTA since 1998. Call (416) 663-8000 or request a free quote.
## 
- 
- 
### 
### 
### 
Questions
## Related questions
Anything not covered here? Call (416) 663-8000 and ask.
Can smoke-damaged brick be cleaned?
Yes. Exterior soot on brick and stone is cleaned with suitable cleaners and controlled washing, or gentle media blasting for heavy deposits.
How quickly should restoration start?
As soon as the property is declared safe and your insurer is notified. Delays let soot, odour and water damage spread.

Questions
# Pressure Washing & Restoration FAQ
Answers to the questions GTA homeowners, property managers and contractors ask us most.
- Since 199828 years in business
- 7,500+properties cleaned
- $5Mliability insured
- WSIBcovered & ISSA-GBAC
- 4.9 / 5rated on Google
## General
How quickly can Living Water start?
Residential jobs are usually booked within 2–5 days, and same-week service is standard. Commercial and industrial clients get 24/7 emergency response on (647) 833-4343.
Are you licensed and insured?
Yes. Living Water is fully licensed in Ontario, carries $5 million in commercial general liability insurance, is WSIB covered and ISSA-GBAC certified. We send a Certificate of Insurance to your property manager, condo board or HOA on request.
Will pressure washing damage my driveway, brick or siding?
Not when it is done right. We match the pressure, nozzle, water temperature and chemistry to each surface — interlock, brick, vinyl, stucco, stone and wood all need different approaches. Where high pressure is wrong we soft wash, steam or use media blasting instead.
Do you do commercial and industrial work?
Yes — refineries, plants, silos and tanks, heritage restoration, graffiti removal, sandblasting and elevator pit cleaning. Many of our clients are property managers, general contractors and municipalities. Our crews are certified boom and scissor lift operators.
What areas do you serve?
Toronto and the entire Greater Toronto Area, including Mississauga, Brampton, Vaughan, Markham, Richmond Hill, Oakville, Burlington, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa, plus Hamilton, Niagara, Guelph, Cambridge, Barrie and Simcoe County.
Is the quote free?
Yes. Assessments are free and no-obligation, and you receive a fixed written quote before any work starts.
## Residential Power Washing
How often should I pressure wash my driveway?
Most GTA homeowners wash driveways and interlock every one to two years, ideally in spring to remove winter salt and again if moss or oil stains appear.
Can you clean my roof without damaging shingles?
Yes. Roofs are soft washed at low pressure with cleaners that kill moss and algae, so granules and shingles are not damaged. We clean cedar, ceramic and metal roofs.
Do I need to be home during the cleaning?
Not usually. We need access to an outdoor water tap and the areas being cleaned. We send before and after photos when the job is complete.
Do you move patio furniture?
Yes. Our crews move and replace patio furniture and protect plants, windows and nearby surfaces as part of the job.
## Commercial Power Washing
Can you work after hours?
Yes. We regularly schedule commercial work overnight and on weekends so tenants, shoppers and staff are not disrupted.
Do you provide a Certificate of Insurance?
Yes. We carry $5 million commercial general liability and full WSIB coverage, and send a COI and WSIB clearance with every quote.
Can you set up a maintenance schedule?
Yes. Many property managers book seasonal or monthly cleaning for entrances, garages and walkways.
## Industrial Power Washing
What is hydro jetting?
Hydro jetting uses very high-pressure water streams to scour build-up from the inside of pipes, condensers and lines without abrasive media.
Do you offer emergency industrial cleaning?
Yes. Industrial and commercial clients can reach our 24/7 emergency line at (647) 833-4343.
Can you clean food processing plants?
Yes. We provide pressure washing, sanitation and disinfection for food plants, scheduled around production.
## Sandblasting & Media Blasting
Is sandblasting safe for brick?
It can be, with the right media and pressure. Soft or heritage brick often needs micro blasting or soda blasting instead of sand. We assess first and test a small area.
What is dustless sandblasting?
Dustless blasting mixes water with the abrasive media so dust is captured at the surface, making it cleaner and safer for occupied or urban sites.
Do you blast swimming pools?
Yes. We blast concrete pool shells to remove failing paint so they can be repainted.
## Brick Cleaning & Paint Removal
Can paint be removed from brick without damaging it?
In most cases, yes. We use chemical strippers and controlled low-pressure rinsing, or gentle media blasting for stubborn coatings, after testing a small area.
What is a brick acid wash?
An acid wash dissolves mortar smears and mineral stains from new or old brick. It must be correctly diluted, tested and neutralised to avoid burning the brick.
Do you clean interior brick?
Yes — interior brick walls and fireplaces can be cleaned with low-moisture methods and full protection of the room.
## Historical Remediation
Which cleaning methods are safe for heritage masonry?
Usually the gentlest effective method: low-pressure steam, poultices, soda or micro blasting at low pressure, and carefully tested chemical cleaners. High-pressure water and coarse sand are avoided on soft historic brick and stone.
Can you remove lead paint?
Yes. We remove lead-based paint from historic surfaces with containment and safe handling and disposal of waste.
Do you work with heritage consultants?
Yes. We regularly work alongside architects, heritage conservators and general contractors and can complete test panels for approval.
## Disaster Restoration
Do you respond to emergencies at night or on weekends?
Yes. Our emergency line, (647) 833-4343, is answered 24/7 for fire, water, wind and commercial emergencies.
Do you work with insurance claims?
We document damage with photos and written scopes that you can provide to your insurer. Contact your insurance company as soon as possible after a loss.
How fast must water damage be dried?
As soon as possible. Mould can begin growing within 24–48 hours, which is why extraction and drying start immediately.
## Elevator Pit Cleaning
How often should a condo clean its elevator pits?
At least once a year, and more often in high-traffic buildings. Many property managers book a cleaning after winter to remove salt and meltwater residue, and immediately after any flood, leak or sewage backup.
Who is responsible for cleaning the elevator pit?
The building owner or property manager usually arranges pit cleaning. The elevator contractor maintains the equipment and controls access, so the cleaning is coordinated with them.
Do you work after hours?
Yes. We regularly schedule overnight, early-morning and weekend pit cleaning so residents and tenants are not inconvenienced.
How long is the elevator out of service?
Routine pit cleaning is usually completed in a few hours per elevator. Flood, oil or sewage clean-ups take longer depending on volume and disposal.
Do you provide insurance and WSIB documents?
Yes. We send our Certificate of Insurance ($5M commercial general liability) and WSIB clearance with every quote.
Can you clean pits in multiple buildings?
Yes. We set up one-time, seasonal or recurring programs across property management portfolios in Toronto and the GTA.
What causes water in an elevator pit?
Common causes are groundwater seepage, failed sump pumps, meltwater and salt slush tracked in during winter, sprinkler discharge, burst pipes and floor-washing water entering the hoistway.
## Efflorescence Removal
What causes efflorescence?
Water dissolves salts inside brick, mortar, concrete or stone, carries them to the surface and evaporates, leaving a white crystalline deposit.
Can pressure washing alone remove efflorescence?
Light, fresh efflorescence sometimes brushes or rinses off, but established deposits usually need a suitable masonry cleaner followed by controlled rinsing.
Is efflorescence covered by my stone warranty?
Many Ontario stone and paver manufacturers use Living Water as their warranty service provider. Check with your supplier or contact us.
## Graffiti Removal
How fast can graffiti be removed?
We typically remove graffiti within the same week, and sooner for offensive tags or commercial clients.
Will the wall show a shadow afterwards?
Fresh graffiti removed with the right chemistry usually leaves no trace. Older tags on porous brick can leave light ghosting, which we minimise with poultices or gentle blasting.
What is an anti-graffiti coating?
A clear protective coating that makes future graffiti easier to remove without damaging the surface underneath.
## Stone Restoration
Can you clean limestone and marble safely?
Yes. Soft, acid-sensitive stones like limestone and marble are cleaned with pH-appropriate products and low pressure — never harsh acids.
Should natural stone be sealed?
Often, yes — especially patios and pool coping. Sealing helps resist staining. We advise based on the stone type and use.
Do you clean monuments and statues?
Yes. Monuments, memorials and statues are cleaned with gentle, conservation-appropriate methods.
## Metal Restoration
Can you remove rust without damaging the metal?
Yes. We select the blasting media and pressure to suit the metal so the substrate is cleaned without unnecessary profile or thinning.
Do you restore architectural copper and aluminium?
Yes — including heritage copper and aluminium elements on historic buildings.
